Using the provided image as the primary reference, first analyze and infer the main subject, theme, emotional tone, and any implied contrast or duality within the image.

Based on the inferred theme, reinterpret and enhance the scene into a high-quality isometric miniature 3D parallel-world diorama, representing two contrasting realities of the same subject (World A vs World B).

Avoid rigid or formulaic composition.
Allow flexible, creative, and varied layouts such as diagonal or curved divisions, offset or layered spaces, foreground–background separation, asymmetric balance, or partially overlapping environments, while still clearly expressing the dual-reality concept.

Preserve the core visual identity, proportions, and spatial logic of the reference image, but allow camera framing, base structure, and internal layout to adapt dynamically and intelligently to the subject.
If a base or platform is present, it may split, step, layer, fracture, or transition organically rather than mirror perfectly.

Apply soft refined textures, realistic PBR materials, and high-quality miniature diorama craftsmanship.
Use clearly contrasting lighting styles, color grading, atmosphere, or environmental cues for each reality, without relying on symmetry or visual clichés.
Include tiny stylized human characters integrated into the environment, without facial details, existing differently in each reality.

Simplify or replace the background with a clean solid color or minimal abstract backdrop that best complements the inferred theme.
If text is included, automatically generate a concise title derived from the inferred subject,
place the subtitle “Parallel Realities” beneath it,
and ensure all text automatically adapts to background contrast (white or black).

Maintain a polished, cinematic, high-end miniature diorama aesthetic with clear depth, consistent scale, strong compositional clarity, and professional presentation quality.
